- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged mean.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates upward momentum in bullish sentiment; add 0.5–1.5% buffer if sentiment > 0.67.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting — anticipate upward correction; add 0.3–0.8% to forecast from midpoint onward.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — sentiment history matters more than daily sentiment alone.
